one_line_contribution: That a ~300-token rule-compiled table of object-to-receptacle placement frequencies, aggregated across the whole expert pool and served as a cached type-agnostic static prefix, carries cross-episode information that top-k retrieved trajectories structurally cannot, and that on ALFWorld's search-bound task types it matches the retrieval gain over no memory at zero uncached prefill and erases the residual that k=3 retains over the best static arm - with derangement, depth-at-fixed-coverage, a no-experience LLM-written table, and a whole-bank-with-and-without-its-own-table pair used to attribute the gain to aggregation rather than to scaffold, coverage, pretraining, or implicit extraction by the reader.
closest_prior_work: Two threats, of different kinds. (1) Closest named method: Dynamic Cheatsheet, arXiv:2504.07952 (verified via s2cli, S2 record: EACL, 113 citations) - a persistent evolving cheatsheet of reusable insights written at test time. It does not threaten the specific claim: its artifact is insight text, not a cross-episode frequency statistic; it never runs a retrieval-of-raw-episodes arm at matched tokens, and it never varies how much experience is compiled. The proposal's characterization of it is accurate. (2) The real threat is to the mechanism, not to the comparison: the embodied/robotics line already establishes that object-receptacle placement statistics drive object search. Verified: arXiv:2607.00022 (PerSim, 'When to Personalize Household Object Search', 2026-06-18, S2, 2 cit) trains room-level priors and within-room co-occurrence cues for household object search; arXiv:2207.10761 (TIDEE) and arXiv:2305.17537 (Scene Graph Memory, object-location prediction in partially observable homes) predate it, and arXiv:2607.14514 (VTM-Nav, 2026-07-16, hf) reuses cross-episode experience for object-goal navigation. Adjacent and worth citing: arXiv:2308.00675 (Tool Documentation Enables Zero-Shot Tool-Usage) already shows a compiled description substituting for demonstrations - the general 'compiled artifact beats retrieved examples' move is not new, only its instantiation as a frequency table against a trajectory retriever is. Against that background, the contribution reduces to the attribution structure (derangement, depth-at-fixed-coverage, LLM-prior, whole-bank pair) rather than the finding that placement statistics help. The proposal's named WCCIS 2026 symbolic-agent paper ('Zero-Shot Embodied Decision Making with Structured Prior Knowledge') is the nearest overlap it identifies, but it has no arXiv id and I could not verify it through the available channel; treat it as unverified.
strongest_objection: The most probable single outcome hollows out the headline. The proposal itself concedes in Limitations that ALFWorld placements are sampled from generic plausibility and are scene-agnostic - which is exactly the condition under which the LLM-prior arm (P4) matches the compiled table. P4 demands that experience beat Qwen3-32B's own same-format, same-vocabulary table by M2 = +7 points on ~30 stereotyped object classes; that is a large ask, and if it fails, 'cross-episode statistics compiled from the bank' collapses to 'write the commonsense placement prior into the prompt', which is a prompt-engineering observation the robotics line (2607.00022, 2207.10761, 2305.17537) and the proposal's own WCCIS reference already assume. The title claim, and the brief's compilation-from-experience framing, would be unsupported by the experiment that was run. A second, compounding objection: the headline P1 is scored against k0, not against static3, even though the round's binding rule makes the best static arm the baseline. cheatsheet_all - static3 is 'reported' but carries no pre-registered margin and no falsifier, so the study cannot fail on the comparison the round exists to force. Third, the entailment check's two near-entailments are acknowledged and then not fixed: with shuffled_all at or below k0, P1 at M1 algebraically delivers P3 at M1, and P7's ceiling scoring of no-take episodes converts P1's success gain directly into the receptacle-count reduction - so of eight predictions, two are re-expressions of the headline, and P8 is a gate whose every branch proceeds with an acceptance band set equal to the noise floor.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Make P4 the headline, not an attribution ablation. The claim worth an ICLR slot is 'compiled experience beats the model's own prior', so cheatsheet_all - LLM_prior should be P1 with the margin, and cheatsheet_all - k0 demoted to a manipulation check; alternatively, plant the divergence - perturb the ALFWorld placement distribution (regenerate or filter games so a subset of object classes sits at non-modal receptacles) and build the bank from the perturbed distribution, giving two levels of prior-experience divergence and turning a named property into a manipulated one. That single change also satisfies the round's 'manipulate, do not observe' rule, which the current design meets only for the artifact, not for the environment property. (2) Attach a pre-registered margin and falsifier to cheatsheet_all - static3 and to the type-agnostic combo instr_all + cheatsheet_all, and run the latter at 8 seeds rather than at 2 seeds with a +/-12 floor - it, not the static3 combo, is the rule-compliant test of P5. (3) Adopt the entailment check's fixes verbatim: set P3's margin at M1 plus the measured shuffled_all - k0 gap (or score it as equivalence of shuffled_all to k0), make P7's both-arms-take restricted version primary, and give P8 a paired-equivalence band from re-run noise plus at least one k3 - k0 branch that stops the run. (4) Add the two arms named under missing_baseline.
missing_baseline: An object-conditioned retriever: k=3 trajectories selected because they contain the target object class, token-matched to k3. The title asserts what retrieval cannot carry, but the plan only runs the goal-sentence retriever from Measurement A, which selects by task type and therefore rarely returns the target object's placements. A trivial string-match retriever over the same 1,465-item pool does deliver placement evidence per query, and it costs one extra arm on hardware that already holds the bank. Without it the claim is not 'retrieval structurally cannot aggregate' but 'this particular retriever does not retrieve placements', and a reviewer will make that substitution in one sentence. Second omission, smaller but load-bearing for the content-vs-scaffold claim: there is no neutral scaffold arm. shuffled_all is an actively misleading table, so cheatsheet_all - shuffled_all confounds 'the right content helps' with 'the wrong content hurts' (the proposal half-sees this and adds only a reading rule). A uniform table - same format, same object classes, every receptacle in the vocabulary listed with no counts or equal counts, token-matched - is the arm that isolates the scaffold. Also absent: the self pool, which the brief names as the on-policy counterpart and which would test whether the statistic survives compilation from the agent's own noisier successes.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. My searches, all through channel (a) the s2cli command (S2 + HF together); WebSearch was unavailable in this session and was not used, so no query was answered by channel (b). Q1 'compiled cross-episode statistics prompt versus retrieval agent memory' --recent: 12 hits, nearest 2603.02473 (retrieval vs write strategy in agent memory), 2605.18421 EvoMemBench (long-context baselines beat specialized memory), 2602.02007 (retrieval by decoupling and aggregation - aggregation over retrieved units, not a compiled static prefix); none compiles a cross-episode statistic and compares it with retrieval. Q2 'object receptacle location frequency table compiled from trajectories ALFWorld LLM agent' (all-time): nothing relevant. Q3 (closest named method) 'Dynamic Cheatsheet test-time learning persistent memory reusable strategies': 2504.07952, plus 2606.05684 AdaMEM, 2512.10696 ReMe, 2509.04439 ArcMemo - all insight/skill memories, none with a raw-retrieval control at matched tokens. Q4 'aggregate statistics across episodes into a prompt instead of retrieving individual trajectories' --recent: 6 hits, nearest 2607.07504 (LLM-generated skills do not reliably beat direct task prompting across thousands of runs - a supporting prior, not a collision). Q5 (home literature, no agent/memory/retrieval words) 'semantic placement prior object goal search co-occurrence statistics household embodied': 2207.10761 TIDEE, 2305.17537 Scene Graph Memory, 2302.12915, 2108.00159, 2607.14514 VTM-Nav - the mechanism is well established outside LLM agent memory, which caps novelty even without a collision. Q6 'compiled playbook fixed prompt versus retrieved trajectories matched token budget agent memory baseline' --recent: 2608.15008, 2605.13880 Preping, 2608.05784 Activity Frames; none runs the matched-token contrast. Q7 'summarized dataset statistics in prompt versus many-shot demonstrations in-context learning aggregation': 2308.00675 (documentation substitutes for demonstrations) is the nearest general precedent for the compiled-beats-examples move. On the proposal's own check: it is above average for this round - three query classes, channels named, IDs given, one query in the home vocabulary without agent/memory words, and a verdict that concedes the mechanism exists in robotics. ID verification: I verified 2504.07952, 2605.24117, 2406.14596, 2511.07800, 2512.23760, 2606.03951 and 2607.00022 through s2cli (all resolve, titles match the proposal's descriptions; note 2406.14596's S2 title is the ICAL NeurIPS paper, as claimed). I could NOT verify 2603.05642, cited as 'SymSearch' and used in the novelty argument to establish that the mechanism exists in robotics - s2cli returns 'not found on S2 or HF'. The WCCIS 2026 paper, which the proposal itself calls its nearest overlap, has no arXiv id and is unverifiable through the available channel; since it is the single closest work by the authors' own account, its unverifiability is a real gap in the novelty case rather than a formality.
